newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka journalists protest for media freedom.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka journalists protest for media freedom.

text.p: Hundreds of Sri Lankan journalists staged a peaceful demonstration in Colombo on Wednesday in protest against a crackdown on the media by the country's security-conscious government.
About 1,000 journalists representing 27 media organisations took part in the protest while two bus-loads of armed police looked on. There were no incidents or arrests.
"It is one of the biggest gatherings of media personnel this country has ever seen," one of the organisers, Saman Wagaarachchi from the Sinhalese-language Lakbima newspaper, told Reuters.
"We're demonstrating for a free media principle and a free media culture in Sri Lanka. We want to insist that the government creates one."
The demonstration was prompted by the detention and charging of a director of the private television station TNL on January 2.
The government accused the director and the station of broadcasting what it said was false news reporting a separatist Tamil guerrilla attack against an eastern army camp.
The government says the attack did not take place.
The director was charged under the Prevention of Terrorism Act and released on bail. The government said the news item could have caused racial tension and endangered security.
Police are also investigating an alleged attack on a Independent Television Network camera crew by a deputy minister's bodyguards on New Year's Day.
Demonstrators on Wednesday carried placards saying the government was using the draconian terrorism act to harass the media.
Government forces are at war with Tamil guerrillas who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this Indian Ocean island's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in is 14th year.
The People's Alliance government won power in 1994 with media freedom one of its main campaign planks.
